analysis.title: Market Update US, Europe & Asia
key_insights: US equities closed mostly lower Friday but well off session lows: S&P 500 -0.40%, Nasdaq -0.91%, Dow +0.10%. Major indices posted solid weekly gains, breadth was positive, and the equal-weight S&P beat the cap-weighted index by more than 60 bp.

Nvidia's board removed Jensen Huang as CEO following revelations of extramarital affairs. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO and Nvidia reportedly approached ARM CEO Rene Haas. The stock fell 11% on the week to its lowest since July 2025, and Nvidia-backed neoclouds came under pressure. AMD and Broadcom are seen as positioned to capture share.

The AI trade was broadly lower (neoclouds, memory, semiconductors). The move was rotation rather than risk-off, with energy and defensives gaining. Treasury yields rose 3-4 bp at the long end, the dollar index rose 0.2% near a fresh 19-month high, and WTI settled -0.2%.

October PPI: headline +0.3% m/m vs +0.4% consensus, core +0.3% in line. September was revised to +1.4% headline and +0.8% core. Annualized headline PPI is 6.5% vs 6.6% consensus, the highest since Nov-22. The cooler print led to downward revisions of October core PCE estimates.

Fed pricing: markets expect a 25 bp hike in December, with a roughly 10-13% chance of 50 bp, and 85 bp of hikes through year-end 2027, up 39 bp w/w. Fedspeak was hawkish (Collins, Goolsbee, Daly, Waller open to 50 bp). Williams said more tightening is needed but sees no overheating.

Oil is heading for a second weekly decline on hopes of a US-Iran stalemate without renewed military conflict. Offsetting factors: continued attacks on Hormuz shipping (36 attacks on commercial vessels in October, most since the war began) and Houthi strikes on Saudi oil infrastructure. The IEA expects a return to surplus this quarter, and OPEC+ output recovered to 97% of pre-war February levels.

Cisco fell 6.2% despite an FQ1 beat and above-consensus FQ2 guidance, as analysts flagged margin pressure from hyperscaler mix. Cerebras rose 11.2% after guiding Q4 well ahead of expectations, with a third hyperscale customer (MSFT cloud agreement). Liftoff Mobile rose 30.6% and Modine rose 27.9% on a Bloomberg report of Samsung acquisition talks.

European equities were mixed: DAX -0.1%, CAC +0.1%, FTSE 100 +0.4%. The STOXX 600 was flat on the day but posted its largest weekly gain in almost four months. The OAT-Bund spread widened to about 154 bps, and the UK 10-year gilt yield rose 2 bp to 5.34%.

Eurozone Q3 GDP was confirmed at +0.4% q/q, double expectations, and UK Q3 GDP was +0.7% q/q, the fastest in more than two years. ECB's Lane said a December hike would be prudent if data are unchanged and that inflation could exceed 4% by year-end. BoE's Lombardelli called December and February live meetings. European gas is above €85/MWh.

UK is reportedly close to a deal with the EU ahead of next week's summit, including UK inclusion in Made in Europe legislation. Putin agreed to European participation in the next US-brokered Ukraine peace talks, but with conditions on European security architecture. Italy's 2027 election race is tight, with the centre-left at 43-45%.

Asian equities fell again Friday. Nikkei, Topix and Taiex were positive, while the Kospi fell. The Hang Seng broke below 24K on Chinese internet and AI stocks, which fell on concerns about tighter US chip export rules. USD/JPY stalled just short of 160 on MOF verbal intervention and a dovish BOJ's Asada.

US lawmakers are moving on four bills to tighten chip exports to China. There is scrutiny of White House ties to Huang and of Commerce Secretary Lutnick, with Reuters reporting officials discussed whether Lutnick should be pushed out. Senate Banking Chair Scott called on Huang and Lutnick to testify next month.

China October activity data is expected to be soft: industrial production 5.3% y/y vs 5.5%, retail sales 0.8% vs 1.1%, and FAI -7.0% YTD. CPCA passenger car sales fell 27% in October, the 13th straight decline. India's October CPI hit a two-year high, breaching the RBI tolerance band.

Hon Hai's Q3 beat consensus. Chairman Liu sees no sign of changing AI demand in the short term and expects high double-digit growth in AI rack shipments q/q and in 2027. Cloud & Networking are over 50% of 2026 revenue.

market_movers.rationale: CEO Jensen Huang removed, Kress named interim CEO. The stock fell 11% on the week to its lowest since July 2025, and succession and AI ecosystem funding concerns weigh.
Fell 6.2% despite an FQ1 beat and above-consensus FQ2 guidance, as analysts flagged margin pressure from rising hyperscaler mix and slowing growth elsewhere.
Rose 11.2% on a Q3 beat, a Q4 guide well ahead of expectations, and a third hyperscale customer.
Rose 27.9% on a Bloomberg report of acquisition talks with Samsung Electronics.
Baird upgraded from neutral on steps toward more balanced sales growth and improving franchisee economics.
Citi downgraded from buy on the lack of another breakout hit and time/attention pressure from the GTA VI launch.
Fell 8.5% after the CFO left for IONQ. Q3 and FY27 guidance were reaffirmed.
Rose 23.8% on a Q3 net income and revenue beat, positive FCF and a raised FY26 guide.
Rose 14.6% on FDA clearance for Tandem Mobi.
Fell 8.0% on a Q3 earnings and margin miss and a cut to FY26 guidance.
Asos upgraded to buy at Peel Hunt after customer growth returned for the first time in four years.
Euronext upgraded at Barclays on fixed-income growth through MTS.
Siemens Energy upgraded at Oddo on an order book of €164B and a plan for €55B cumulative FCF by 2030.
Enel downgraded at Santander because expected EPS growth relies on M&A and buybacks and on regulatory and political risks.

sector_views.rationale: Energy and defensives gained in the US rotation, and European oil and gas and utilities outperformed.
AI-linked names (semis, memory, neoclouds, software, networking) lagged in the US, and tech lagged in Europe on AI doubts.

earnings_insights: Cisco FQ1 EPS and revenue beat, FQ2 guidance above consensus, FY27 AI revenue outlook raised. The stock fell 6.2% on hyperscaler margin concerns.
Cerebras Q3 beat. It guided Q4 materially ahead of expectations and reiterated about 3x FY27 revenue growth.
Liftoff Mobile reported a Q3 beat with revenue better, and Q4 and FY26 guidance ahead of the Street.
Flowers Foods Q3 earnings and adjusted EBITDA margin missed, revenue in line, FY26 guidance cut.
Hon Hai Q3 headline metrics beat consensus, with AI rack shipments expected to grow at a high double-digit rate q/q and in 2027.

Richemont's Q2 group sales were a modest beat, but Jewellery Maisons growth was slower than expected (reported). ams-OSRAM guided Q4 revenue to €750-850M, with the €800M midpoint below the €829M consensus.

CTS Eventim Q3 revenue of €809.1M missed the €846.7M estimate, and adjusted EBITDA of €133.8M missed the €138.1M estimate. Enel's nine-month ordinary EBITDA of €17.95B and ordinary net income of €6.02B beat consensus.
Generali 9M adjusted net income of €3.68B beat the €3.56B consensus. Land Securities H1 EPRA EPS of 25.9p beat the 25.2p estimate.

risk_factors: Nvidia leadership vacuum and its role as a source of funds for the AI ecosystem, including Nvidia-backed neoclouds.
Tighter US chip export rules affecting Chinese tech and AI names.
Hawkish Fed repricing, including a possible 50 bp hike in December.
Energy shock lifting inflation and hawkish ECB and BoE rhetoric. KPMG warned further shocks could undermine the UK recovery.
Yen intervention risk near 160 per dollar.
US-Iran military escalation and attacks on Hormuz shipping.
France's fiscal and political uncertainty weighing on sovereign spreads.
vol_and_positioning: The Volatility index row is in the market barometer, but its values are blank in the text.

OAT-Bund spread widened to about 154 bps as the French 10-year yield rose 8 bp vs 3 bp for Bunds.
geopolitical: US-Iran stalemate hopes are pressing oil lower, but Hormuz shipping attacks continue (36 attacks on commercial vessels in October, the most since the war began) and Houthis struck Saudi oil infrastructure.
Putin agreed to European representatives joining US-brokered Ukraine peace talks but is demanding a redesigned European security architecture and warned against Western troops in Ukraine.
UK is close to an EU reset deal ahead of next week's summit, including inclusion in Made in Europe legislation.
US lawmakers are moving four bills to tighten chip exports to China, and Beijing warned against a 'tech blockade'.
Scrutiny of Commerce Secretary Lutnick over chip diversions to China, with Reuters reporting talk of pushing him out.
Italy's 2027 election race is near a dead heat between the two main coalitions.

tension_points.bull_case: Williams said the economy does not appear overheated, the labor market is strengthening, and the cooler headline PPI led to lower October core PCE estimates, which supports a 25 bp rather than 50 bp December move.
tension_points.bear_case: Waller is open to 50 bp in December in a hotter scenario, and Goolsbee and Collins flag broadening inflation. Daly's bias for rates is up. Markets priced 85 bp of hikes through year-end 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hotter inflation print that makes a 50 bp December hike more likely, as Waller described.

tension_points.bull_case: Hon Hai's chairman sees no sign of changing AI demand, Cerebras guided Q4 well ahead, and AMD and Broadcom are positioned to capture any share gain.
tension_points.bear_case: Huang's removal, the lack of succession planning, and Nvidia's role as a source of funds for neoclouds raise concern about the AI ecosystem.
